Contest of Themes!

This is my first time, so don't go hard on me.

This contest is a mapmaking/judging/contest.
but with a twist.

I think of a theme (or suggest it if you want.) of a type of map you make.
The judges will play the game and based on the gamplay, aesthtetics(flow), and fun, with the scoring chart below.

gameplay-n/10
aesthetics-n/10
flow-n/5

When all the judges have . . . judged, I will calculate the mean score of all the judges, and that will be their score, adding each mean of each submitted map. Wow.

Rules!

@ No using maps already made on NUMA. You have to start fresh.
@ Judges may submit, but under the supreme rule of the head judge.
@ Anyone can join, but only 5 can be judges (including me), due to the fact that I won't be going up and down for 50 judges.
@ Any one can join at any point, but they will have to start with 0.
@ Each round lasts 6 days, so no worries.
@ (to judges) no harsh judging, constructive critism needed.
@ (to mapmakers) you can only submit 3 maps per round.
@ The Suprme Judge (me) will have to multiply the score by 4 with the judges that submit their maps and continue with the same process. A bit complicated, but I have a calculator in my hand.

And thats it.

1st place - Uber sigtag & matching uber avatar
2nd place- Uber sigtag & matching awesome avator
3rd place - Sigtag & avatar

1st round starts June 8 - ends at June 14

Judges, PM your judging to me.

Mapmakers-Submit Your maps to NUMA, with the link to your map here.

Quote: Demonized, 2007-09-03T21:55:23Z
Freezing time, as long as I don't age when I stop it.

You've seen too much "Click" people. It's just a movie...

Anyway, my power would be Electromagentic creation/control. Basically, you can create electricity wtihin your own fingertips and move anything magnetic (which involves a whole lotta things.) You can even transfer electricity and even control and electrical machine.

Say you're in a desert. You are 2,000 miles from civilization, and next to you is a telephone wire. There are so many ways to escape.

*Using the magnetic feild of earth to fly by using the opposite electromagnetic pole (positive or negative.) It's like anti-gravity, but it's not.

*Create an electromagnetic current to the ground and "push" yourself, causing you to go at a high rate of speed. Once you land, you stop yourself with the earth's polar opposite electromagnetic field (see above) and stop. Repeat untill you've reached your destination.

#17555 1 2007-10-14T23:33:42Z Animator
This guide will teach you how to use different ways of using the animation software Pivot Stickfigure Animator to it's full potential and capabilities.

First, download it.

Link.

This is Pivot 3 beta. This one I recommend to be used based on the fact that it has a much nicer display, allows more than 1 background to be used, and allows sprites.
Spoiler: Beginners GuideNow, on to the actual animation. Open it up, and know I shall teach.

Regular animation:

This is the most basic style of animation used in this program. You will need:

-An imaging program (i.e. paint, photoshop, GIMP, etc.)

-Using the image program, make a background (any, I don't care.)
-Save your background as a .jpeg or .bitmap or .GIF (use bitmap better, image has better view.)
-Go to File, then Load Background.
-Look around for the background you made, and click on it. Make sure it is any of the 3 types of file I stated, or you can't use it.

And you have a background. (you could also get an image from the internet, save it as any 3 files I stated, and put it in there.)

Here is a sample background. If it ever asks you to change the size dimensins of the animation to the background, say yes.



Now, on to the stick figures.

You can either:
a) Use the default one.
b) Make one yourself.

If you chose a), skip this.

When you make a stickfigure, there are many options to keep mind of.



-Creates a new pivot stick. Just connect it with a red dot on your stickfigure.



-Creates a circle, moslty used for heads and wheels and etc.



-Makes a stick skinner or thicker, depending on your concept of a particular character.



-This duplicates a stick (any) you may have selected. It will be then duplicated in the exact size and postion. Good for creating even legs and arms.



-This is probably the most powerful instument. When you have selected a stick, press this button, and the stick must stay in that postion. The effects can ONLY be seen in the actual animation set-up. In edit mode, it will only appear grey, signifying that this will be a frozen stick. Use this when you have a stick limb that is not needed to be moved.



-The delete button. Select a stick, press this button, and delete it. Warning: You can only delete sticks by the one that is the most outside, not the ones in the center. There is 1 master stick that cannot be destroyed.

Once you've finished your figure, be sure you have it perfectly made with no mistakes. Save it, and then click "Add to Animation" in file.

Now the most important part: Frames.

Add your stickfigure by clicking on the stickfig's name in the list next to you. There are various things to do with it.

Delete

If you have spare stickfigures, select them by clicking on the red dots (or pivots) and press the delete button.

Edit

Use this if it didn't come out how you think it would, and then fix it.

Center

Centers the stickfigure.

Flip

Flips the stickfigure into a mirror image... literally.

Colour

You can actually change the color of the stickfigure into whatever you like. Pink, blue, red, green, anything. But it has to be 1 solid color.

Size lever

When you see a number (usually 100) in an option box, it can resize the stickfigure into whatever you want.

Front and back

This option usually applies when there is more than 1 stickfigure. Choose a specific stickfigure. Front makes him shown to the front, and back makes it go to the back, not to be seen.

Once you have your frame prepared, click on the next frame button to make another frame. Notice that when you move the stickfigure, a grey shadow of it appears. That is for keeping track of it's earlier position (much like a claymation, only easier.) Remeber that the more frames you have, the more smooth the animation appears.Once you are done, your animation should at least resemble a smooth animation like this:



You can always control the speed.





Choose the speed that best fits your animation. If there is a mistake in a frame, then go to the bad frame by clicking on one of the frames at the top, and edit it.

Always save it as a .*GIF (animated .GIF) A menu will pop out, with a resize option. Make sure the resize option is at 100%, or else, your animation will be shrunken or enlarged.

Upload it in Imageshack, and show it off.
Spoiler: Sprite animation.
Sprite animation. The animation software at it's best. You will need:

-Imaging software (paint recommended)
-Pivot open.
-A huge determination.

First, open pivot, with a background.

Here's mine:



Go look for a spritesheet. Google is your friend.

Now, here is the very complicated part. Transparency is allowed on characters only. If there is pure white in your character, replace it with a white substitute (1 pixel difference of white.)

I'll use this. Remeber to credit those whos sprites you use. They will get you.

http://rmc.technoized.com/sprites/misc-sp-dancingbanana.png

Place each sprite in a seperate program (ergo, 5 sprites in 5 paint programs.)

Save your edited sprites as a .gif or .bitmap

Edit them with the least spce that you can. The pivot points will be automatically placed as a pivot stick; 1 pivot spot in one corner and another in an opposite corner.

Add the first part of the sprite, click next frame, delete it, add the next sprite, repeat. It took me 15min. for 1 with this one, based on the fact that to make the animation realistic, you must place the the figure to the exact pixel of where it was earlier.

Once you are done (and credite the person who made the sprite), pick a good, flowy speed to show it off.

And then you're done!


I will add some more guides, like implementing sprite animation, and animated backgrounds, as well as dramatic gradients (seen in movies.)

-All are action, but some are quite easy, while others are challenging whether you go with AGD or not.
-Each map has it's corresponding letter in the beginning of the sentence (which is why half of the maps titltles start with non-captilalized.)
-All maps are made by me. Every single one.
-Some I posted on NUMA for a preview, such as YMCA.

And...

Could you explain what you did a bit more thoroughly Animator? I'm afraid I don't quite follow your logic.

This will be as clear as I will be. The row on 1 side (with the long division sign) is the row to simplify 2 or more shapes. The row on another (the one that splits shapes) is to create more shapes.

Think of a fraction problem. When you add, the denominators must be the same. To best hand;e this problem, you must change the question (or division problem) with almost the same shape. Once you have that down, all you have to do is use the table to simplify each shape from both sides of the equation (or to divide) and you get an answer. The work is not done. Remeber that you must simplify your answer when dealing with fractions. The same goes here. The confusing part is, where you multiply, you may also work backwards and simplify. You must simplify to the point where you reach the prime factor (ergo, to a point where it's impossible to simplify anymore) and you keep your answer.

It's all a theory of mathematical equations, really. Nothing people from college couldn't handle, and I'm from middle school.

Quote: Mosh, 2007-11-19T00:02:34Z
Since drones depend on checking whether or not the tile in front of their path is alright for traveling into before they make one more "step", this wouldn't work. Invisible tile-like objects wouldn't work, because drones detect "solid" objects (tiles and closed/locked doors) to determine their pathing, and not any objects whatsoever. Drone paths aren't predefined, so the engine code upon which Drone's operate on would have to be rewritten.
It's possible, and it's a nice idea, but would require extensive coding to pull off.

Yup. An image contest. The reason? I'm making a magazine about imaging and animation for computer class, and I think it could profit a lot if it included a section devoted to the images of others. Since there are many digital artists here, I thought, "Let me give this place a chance." The requirements:

-The image must be smaller than 1/5 of a regular page.
-You must post your real name, you may PM it to me privately, it only has to be a first name. (If chosen.)
-It must be fit for 13 year-olds. Not 16, 20, or 35 year olds. It's freestyle, but choose your theme wisely.
-Must be .png.
-In the event that there are more than 5 images, I will hold a poll(s) to see which image is more popular. The first top 5 will be chosen from that poll.
-The images are due this Tuesday.

Along with being credited in the magazine, your prize will be:
-A sig set made complete from me.
-A sig tag that says, "I'm famous!".
-A PM'd copy of the magazine. (Do not show to any other forumer.)

And that's it.

Let me explain. I've hit the golden mark of 100 drones (fan-made) and I want to celebrate it with a contest. I'm stuck with 2 ideas.
Spoiler: Drones at Random comic competition:
-You are allowed to make 1 comic based on exactly 20 drones from the last edition of Drones At random (the last 100 drones.)
-You can also make up to 4 comics, but the drones cannot be repeated (thus forcing the player to use all 100.)The best one will be considered.
-Fan drones are allowed (i.e. Master drone, Kenny, any drone non-D.A.R. related), but they won't count
with the total of 20 drones in a comic.
-It's pretty much freestyle, but do comply with the forum rules.
-Can be as many panels as you please/require.
-Judging is as follows:
=Well made: x/5.
=Has 20 drones (exact): x/5.
=Has humor: x/10.
=Overall: x/20.
-Score will be determined in percents. (i.e. 65%.)


Pros of the contest:
-You can make some awesome comics, with the variety of drones.
-Judging is simple.
-The drones will be found easily.( When I post the spritesheet up, of course.)

Cons:
-Way too many drones can equal not enough ingenuity for a comic.

or...
Spoiler: Drones at Random Drone Contest:
-Make a drone, only a drone. Floor guards may be allowed.
-Can be any drone you wish, this contest is freestyle. Comply with the forum rules.
-It must be .png and the limit is 100px. by 100px. Enough space for a drone.
-Allowed to submit up to 3 drones. The best one will be considered.
-It cannot be a drone stolen from my Drones thread, Ignate's spritesheet, the Screen shots of N+, or any drone from N, as well as any other drone thread here. If this is found out, you will be immediately kicked from the competition.
-Your drone must be made from scratch, or you may get an inspiration and edit the regular N drone, but it must be completely and totally different.
-Judging is as follows:
=Aesthetics: x/10.
=Detail: x/5
=Innovation: x/5
=Overall: x/20
-Score will be as a percent. (i.e. 98%).

Pros:
-Very simple and fun.
-Don't have to be an image expert to do this.

Cons:
-This could be a very easily cheated contest (unless you have every single link of a fan drone.)

So... decide.

#19886 1 2008-04-11T00:59:11Z Animator
Answer the poll, for a little experiment. There are many reasons a person may not rate someone's map, and that hurts the flow of NUMA, as explained here:

http://metanet.2.forumer.com/index.php?sho...ndpost&p=460542

And so, for each option, here's what you should do to improve.

1. A map can be messy or sloppy, but that doesn't define the actual map in perspective. You could play this map, and it might result in an overly fun/hilarious situation. If the gameplay wasn't good, then rate it, but always explain comments. Comments are just as important as rates, because it tells what you should improve. Harsh criticisms or not, you should always take it in mind.

2. You -should- care, really. The unrated situation is a self-feeding paradox. If you don't rate (and/or comment), this will indicate that either the regular mapmaker doesn't know what is wrong and will continue creating such atrocious maps (thus causing good maps going away from the attention they deserve), the mapmaker will embrace it as good intentions and will continue (still causing the good maps to go down), or the mapmaker will just quit (which means we would have lost a potential member to our forums), and they all don't end that well. If you took the time to do these comments and rates, you might have inspired a future great mapmaker to improve themselves, thus causing an even more contribution of such professionally well done maps to NUMA.

3. Some people have this problem, really. Worried about such rates, that they forget that NUMA is not a 'get-rated-highly-and-get-popular' community. NUMA is not a competition (which is really what it has all boiled down to). Some people take this too seriously, and will go to no lengths to get rated (which explains the sudden jumps in sniping, multi-accounting, and maybe even no ratings). Just a word in advice: It's just a game. It's not real. You will not win anything of worth if your map becomes the top rated of all of NUMA. Not even dronies count here; It's digital, you're not goona print the thing and hang it, are you? Psh.

4. Rating specific authors is nice, because you get to enjoy your maps with 99.9% certainty that you'll like it. But you need to cut some slack for those other maps, too, you know. They make it with -your- intentions to rate and play.

5. Like I said in poll explanation #2, it all bares down to competition. Snipes lower rates, and that's bad to do. Rate honestly, people. Even it is the person you least enjoy, rate honestly. Maybe you might improve them in a turn for the better.

6. Now, this goes down in either competition, a grudge, or jealousy. If it is a competition, please refer to poll explanation #3. If it is a grudge, then you should just put that aside, man. An eye for an eye would make the world blind. Ghandi said that, and Ghandi ain't never wrong. Just rate the map, and put your hatred aside. You'll be friendly and happy again. Such anger should never become like this. If it is jealousy, then don't be jealous, man. The mapmaker never did anything to you, so why hate him? Rate and comment honestly, man, and all is well.

7. Pardon the bad pun. Explain if you have a different reason.

#428052 5 2008-04-13T14:56:50Z Animator
No. I'll you why.

Say you saved 5 pennies a day, everyday. Now, multiply that by the amount of days in a year, and you get
$18.25. Now, say you continued such a trend, for, oh say, 8 years. You would have $146.00. That means, if you started saving from age 8, in 9 years, you would have some walking money so you'd hang with your friends at the mall. But this is besides the point.

The point is, if pennies didn't exist, then exact amounts (like $14.21) couldn't be calculated, because there's no penny. It's like taking out every hundredth of a decimal (excluding nickels, but that's another story). Since pennies go by the numeric value of .01, then any amount can be possible and calculated. If the penny -was- taken out, then this could only result in an increase of prices (since now, they can only go by fives. Ex: $13.51 could become $13.55) which might affect gas prices (ex. $3.21 might be $3.25). But, there may be another way: it might decrease because of lack of pennies (ex. $14.24 might go down to become $14.20, and with gas prices, $3.23 might go down to $3.20). Knowing our government, of course, the former (not the latter) might occur more likely.

So yeah, pocket change is important.

Well, since I'm new here, with nothing more than a taste for music, a music editor, and 2 years of music class, that I may not be in league with many people here. When I entered this sub forum, I wanted to witness a place filled with buzzing musical action and power, and beautiful musical compositions seen all throughout the land. Now, I only see the later here. I may have been here for only 5 minutes, that is true, but I wanted to envision Metastra as something more than a small project for a game. And Lo, Metastra should not only be for Knytt, as we could extend our things to projects as far as our own radio channel, maybe a soundtrack to N, maybe for music videos, anything beyond such a limited thing. Why should we hold against our talents to only 1 thing here, one project? We are the few, the proud, the Metastra, and we can make musical magic to as much as we desire! Which is why, as an editor, I want to bring back Metastra's glory with guitars, drums, pianos, everything worth performing, and exceed our limits! This of which, as of right here, right now, I want to suggest something that could make Metastra worth more than a small project, I want it to variate with more kinds of projects than it could ever imagine, because nothing is more beautiful than the music in here. I've heard Borealis, Maestro, Lenny, and most other people, and it is a work of art. So now, I want to cast the first stone, to help make something better than what it is now. We should work on different projects (once we finish this one, of course, hell, we could even sidetrack with 2 at the same time. We have enough people, but maybe 2/3rds of them are inactive, from what I've heard) and kick this thing back up. I love Metastra. That is all I have to say.

-Animator

#461189 149 2008-08-17T01:16:07Z Animator
I dunno if this has already been suggested, but a teleportation drone. It could very much simplify teleports, with a demonstration (with words, no pictures. D:)

Say you wanted to teleport to 2 different spaces (Space A and Space B), and you wanted to implement a teleportation method for it. The drone (which could be a light color), when made contact with the ninja, will teleport him to the nearest teleport drone available, locating him to Space B. Instead of depending on a launchpad with varying speeds that could potentially kill you, this teleporter can get you safely to where you want., guaranteed.

Now, here comes the argument of wanting more teleporters. This system could work by the alphabet, in a sense ( A to B to C and so on), or even create new chains of teleporters ( A to B, A1 to B1 to C1, so on).

It would be incredible to see this implemented, because not only does it simplify an existing method of teleportation, it could also bring up some very interesting maps because of it's diversity to allow different chains at once.

So yeah, there's my 2 cents, paid with 4 half-pennies.

Quote: Bubba, 2008-09-05T13:20:25Z
Has anyone else found a glitch where the ninja should be facing the opposite direction but it's not? Like when you are sliding towards a thump that goes left, the ninja is facing right and is few pixels apart from the object... I found it about 1-2 weeks ago.

I found it out today. That being, I just got it today!

There are 2 glitches that worry me, and it's the laser drone invisible line, and the bounce block physics. I may have a probable explanation to what causes the laser line to disappear, as the line is too thin and when aligned at certain angles, it just disappears (I blame the pixel quality), but I don't find it as problematic as I just picture the line in my mind where the laser splash effect goes and just dodge it completely. What really bothers me is the bounce blocks. I never really had a problem with them until I hit the 30's column and met a map made completely of bounce blocks, wall jump-able by each side, with the exit button in the middle. To wall jump on a bounce block is like trying to open a banana with your feet (it's almost impossible, yet feasible). This bothers me, as the slightest slip will kill you, and you're wall jumping on oil that doesn't stick. The music was horrible (except for a few tunes which I liked), but I just muted it out and just grabbed my iPod.

With that out of the picture, I enjoyed it. I really enjoyed it, and I even have my DS next to me making a level and going to upload it into the community. What I wasn't expecting was when I was scrolling down the manual to the credits page, I saw that I had not one level in the DS version, but 2. I was ecstatic when I saw this (It's 6-0 and 23-0, apparently), and there are probably more people who made more than one level on their version, so if you have, don't forget to check out that credits page in the manual. The game was mostly easy, seeing as this was probably aimed at those that never played N before, but there were some elaborately genius maps in it. I looked in the community, and as to my surprise, I saw some maps pertaining to the original N. Overall, I loved it (and the T-shirt. It's my size!)
